full_text_en:
Shi Quan v. Deng Guofen — Dispute over Personal Injury Compensation

Plaintiff: Shi Quan, male, born on January 26, 1935, retired cadre of Hainan Seismological Bureau.

Agent ad litem: Fu Wen and Li Hongwen, lawyers of Zhongtian Law Firm.

Defendant: Deng Guofen, female, born on September 1, 1949, unemployed, currently under treatment at Hainan Anning Hospital due to paranoid schizophrenia.

Legal Representative: Shi Yifeng, born on April 25, 1978, son of Deng Guofen.

Agent ad litem: Chen Fangli, lawyer of New Oriental Law Firm.

The plaintiff, Shi Quan, filed a lawsuit with the Zhendong District People's Court of Haikou City, Hainan Province, against the defendant, Deng Guofen, regarding a dispute over personal injury compensation.

Plaintiff's Allegations: The defendant, Deng Guofen, attacked me with a knife and caused injuries. During hospitalization, medical expenses totaling over RMB 20,000 were incurred. A second surgery on my left arm will cost approximately RMB 10,000. I request the court to order the defendant to pay medical expenses of RMB 40,000 and mental damages of RMB 5,000.

Defendant's Defense (by Legal Representative): The defendant attacked the plaintiff while suffering from paranoid schizophrenia and unable to recognize the consequences of her actions. The expenses incurred during the plaintiff's treatment have already been paid from the community property of the family. The plaintiff's current claim for damages is factually unfounded and should be dismissed.

The Zhendong District People's Court of Haikou City found the following facts upon trial: In the early morning of May 26, 1997, the defendant, Deng Guofen, struck the sleeping plaintiff, Shi Quan, thirteen times with a knife. The forensic examination conclusion (No. [1997] 156 of Haifa Examination) issued by the Haikou Public Security Bureau confirmed that Shi Quan's injuries constituted serious bodily harm. The appraisal conclusion (No. [1997] 17 of Haisi Appraisal) issued by the Hainan Provincial Judicial Psychiatric Appraisal Committee confirmed that Deng Guofen suffered from paranoid schizophrenia and lacked criminal responsibility for the act. During Shi Quan's hospitalization for the knife wounds, medical expenses totaling RMB 9,265.28 were incurred, all of which were paid from the community property of the spouses.

It was also found that prior to May 26, 1997, Deng Guofen had exhibited multiple instances of abnormal behavior, the causes of which were unknown to her family members. On June 17, 1997, Shi Quan filed for divorce on the grounds of a breakdown of marital affection. The Zhendong District People's Court of Haikou City rendered a judgment on September 5, 1997, granting the divorce between Shi Quan and Deng Guofen. During the trial of this case, Shi Quan amended his claims, seeking an additional RMB 5,000 in medical expenses.

The above facts are confirmed by the inpatient fee receipts from Haikou People's Hospital, the forensic examination conclusions from Haikou Public Security Bureau, the appraisal opinions from the Hainan Provincial Judicial Psychiatric Appraisal Committee, and the statements of both parties, which have been examined and verified during trial and may serve as the basis for determining the facts of this case.

The Zhendong District People's Court of Haikou City held that: The plaintiff, Shi Quan, and the defendant, Deng Guofen, were originally husband and wife. During the existence of the marital relationship, Deng Guofen, due to an episode of paranoid schizophrenia, injured Shi Quan while unable to recognize the consequences of her actions. The expenses incurred during Shi Quan's hospitalization had already been paid from the community property of the spouses. Shi Quan's current claim for medical expenses and mental damages lacks factual and legal basis and therefore cannot be supported. Accordingly, on February 12, 1998, the court rendered the following judgment:

Judgment: Reject all claims of the plaintiff, Shi Quan.

Court acceptance fee: RMB 1,610, to be borne by the plaintiff.

After the first-instance judgment was pronounced, Shi Quan, dissatisfied, appealed to the Haikou Intermediate People's Court, arguing that the original judgment was factually unclear and erroneously dismissed his claims. He requested that the original judgment be reversed and that the appellee, Deng Guofen, be ordered to pay RMB 41,323.28 in medical expenses and mental damages.

The Haikou Intermediate People's Court found the following facts upon trial: The appellant, Shi Quan, and the appellee, Deng Guofen, voluntarily registered their marriage on October 11, 1993. After marriage, Deng Guofen developed a mental illness due to emotional stimulation. During the existence of their marital relationship, Deng Guofen had no personal property apart from her equal right to manage the community property of the spouses. After being injured by Deng Guofen, Shi Quan incurred medical expenses of RMB 9,265.28 during hospitalization, of which RMB 6,700 was paid from the community property. After the court granted their divorce on September 5, 1997, Shi Quan filed this personal injury compensation lawsuit in the same month. Apart from the above, the facts found at second instance were consistent with those found at first instance.

The Haikou Intermediate People's Court held that: The appellant, Shi Quan, and the appellee, Deng Guofen, were originally husband and wife. Deng Guofen, suffering from paranoid schizophrenia, injured Shi Quan while unable to recognize the consequences of her actions and lacked criminal responsibility. Article 13 of the Marriage Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Property acquired during the existence of a marital relationship shall be jointly owned by the husband and wife, unless otherwise agreed by the parties." Shi Quan and Deng Guofen had no agreement regarding property, and Deng Guofen had no personal property apart from her equal right to possess and manage the community property. This determines that Deng Guofen lacked the prerequisite and material basis for compensating damages arising between the spouses. After Shi Quan was injured by his wife, Deng Guofen, during the existence of the marital relationship, most of the treatment expenses were paid from the community property. At the time of divorce, the community property was divided according to the respective circumstances of the parties (including Shi Quan's injury). After the divorce, the parties had no further contact. Therefore, Shi Quan's post-divorce claim for personal injury compensation arising during the marriage, seeking payment from the property Deng Guofen received upon divorce, lacks factual and legal basis. The facts found by the original trial were substantially correct, and the judgment was not improper. Shi Quan's grounds of appeal cannot be sustained and should be dismissed according to law. Accordingly, on August 31, 1998, the Haikou Intermediate People's Court, pursuant to Article 153, paragraph 1, item 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment:

Judgment: Dismiss the appeal of the appellant, Shi Quan, and affirm the original judgment.
